NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the pinnacle of the AI computing value chain as a fabless semiconductor company, designing cutting-edge GPUs and networking chips that are manufactured almost exclusively by TSMC using advanced nodes, with critical memory inputs from Micron and SK Hynix. Its downstream is dominated by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) and enterprise OEMs who are in an unprecedented arms race to procure NVIDIA's AI accelerators, giving NVIDIA extraordinary pricing power and making it a chokepoint in global AI infrastructure buildout.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless' designer that outsources manufacturing to a concentrated network of Asian suppliers — most critically TSMC for chips and Samsung/Sony for displays and sensors — while distributing finished products through telecom carriers, major retailers, and its own direct channels worldwide. Its downstream relationships are uniquely powerful, as Apple captures extraordinary margin and also generates significant Services revenue (App Store, licensing) from the installed base of devices sold through those channels.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of the semiconductor value chain, heavily dependent on a concentrated group of capital equipment suppliers (ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research) for its vertically integrated DRAM and NAND manufacturing operations. On the demand side, Micron is increasingly tied to AI-driven workloads, with hyperscalers and NVIDIA representing growing revenue concentration as HBM and high-capacity server DRAM displace commodity memory in its mix.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM sits at a unique and central position in the global semiconductor supply chain as a pure-play IP licensor, dependent primarily on EDA software vendors upstream to develop and verify its CPU/GPU IP cores, while its downstream licensees span virtually every major semiconductor company and hyperscaler that designs chips for mobile, cloud, automotive, and IoT applications. Because ARM licenses its architecture rather than manufacturing silicon, its upstream cost base is relatively lean (R&D tooling focused), while its downstream revenue is broadly diversified across royalties and licensing fees from hundreds of companies building on its instruction set architecture.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology operates as a fabless semiconductor company, sitting between advanced foundry partners (primarily TSMC) and large-scale hyperscaler and OEM customers who embed its data infrastructure chips into data centers, storage systems, and networking equipment. Its strategic position is increasingly critical as it expands into custom AI silicon and high-speed optical/electrical networking, making it a key enabler of cloud and AI infrastructure buildouts for major hyperscalers like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft.
